chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Inform me about the thief, why is his right hand and his left leg cut, and not his right hand and right leg?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'How good is what you asked. If his right hand and right leg were cut, he would fall on his left side and would not be able to stand. But if his right hand and left leg are cut, he balances and stands upright.'

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and how can he stand when his leg is cut?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The cutting is not from where you think. Rather, the leg is cut from the ankle, and what remains of his foot allows him to stand, to pray and worship Allah.'
I said to him, 'From where is the hand cut?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The four fingers are cut, and the thumb is left, so he can depend on it during prayer and wash his face with it for prayer.'
I said, 'So this cutting, who was the first to cut in this manner?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Uthman ibn Affan approved it for Muawiya.'
ai.seo_question: Why is the thief's right hand and left leg cut specifically, and how is the cut performed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential wisdom (hikmah) behind the specific anatomy of the hadd punishment, emphasizing that the cutting occurs distal to the joints to preserve the thief's capacity for standing, prayer, and ablution. It further provides a historical note attributing the refinement of this method to Uthman ibn Affan for Mu'awiya, highlighting the practical application of divine law in maintaining the offender's dignity and ability to worship post-punishment.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Hilal, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Inform me about the thief, why is his right hand and his left leg cut, and his right hand and his right leg is not cut?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How good is what you have asked. When his right hand and right leg is cut, he would fall upon his left side, and he would not be able to stand. So when his right hand and his left leg are cut, he would balance and be able to stand straight’.

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! And how can he stand and his leg has been cut?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The cutting is not from where you view as him being cut. But rather, the man would be cut from the lower part of the foot, and there would be left from his foot upon which he can stand to Pray and worship Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘From where would the hand be cut?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The four fingers would be cut, and the thumb would be left, so he can depend upon it during the Prayer, and he can wash his face with it for the Prayer’.
I said, ‘So this is the cutting from the first one who was cut (in such a manner)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It was Usman Bin Affan who made that good for Muawiya’.
